options.what: `<header class="bg-paper">` → `<header class="bg-tint">`. Type, gaps, the h1 and the name count are untouched.
options.surfaces: One device, one token. This design language separates surfaces by GROUND, not by a drawn line - there is no border in `src/` at all, and a painted 1px hairline is a gate FAIL. `tint` is ratified as a hover fill that carries ink (10.96) and never gold (4.39 = FAIL), so using it as a persistent band extends a role rather than adding a colour: it needs a line in DESIGN.md and a `token-map` entry. Cheapest row in the round - one class.
options.gate: Passes `check:render` untouched (no nav, control or band rule is touched; `tint` is not a dark ground, so the one-dark-band rule is not reached). `check:ground` re-reads the page grounds and would report the second light band; a keyline across the edge is what would trip its straddle rule, and this option draws none.

options.title: the bar gets a warm ground: the tint's lightness and chroma, gold's hue
options.what: `<header class="bg-paper">` → a candidate `--w-warm: oklch(95% .03 62)` — the same L and C as `tint`, hue moved from 152° (the ink family) to 62° (gold’s hue). Nothing else moves.
options.surfaces: The like-for-like answer to "swap the aqua for amber": identical weight, opposite temperature. It is not a new token in @theme, so it is priced as a `--w-*` candidate exactly as round 9 namespaces candidates (D129). What it does to the roles is what the record measures: ink still clears (10.81), but `gold` on it is 4.33 and `rule` is 2.70 — both under their bars, and worse than on tint (4.39 / 2.74). Warmth is not free in a palette whose only boundary role is `rule`.
options.gate: The `tint` role extension is the same one `chrome-ground` needs (a DESIGN.md line + a `token-map` entry), plus a new candidate token the operator has to ratify or reject. No keyline is drawn, so `check:ground`'s straddle rule is not reached.

options.label: chrome-ink-warm
options.title: the ground stays paper; the bar’s ink is warmed to gold's hue
options.what: The bar keeps `bg-paper`; a class `ink-warm` on the header re-declares `--color-ink`, `--color-ink-2`, `--color-ink-3` and `--color-rule` inside the bar at hue 62 instead of 152. Same lightness, same chroma, warmth instead of teal. No ground change.
options.surfaces: This is the direct answer to "that odd teal": the bar is not teal by accident, it is `ink`, and every ink in the palette sits at hue 152. Warmed ink on paper measures 12.37 (cool ink 12.02) - legibility is not the problem. The problem is D88: warm ink at L 32 C .045 H 62 lands 0.063 OKLab from UPS brown #351C15, inside the 0.135 commerce-brand zone. And the reserved join-path hues move closer to it: discord (35°) is 27° away and mobilizon (105°) is 43° away, under the >=47° separation `src/styles/global.css` writes for the path hues. Warming ink is a palette ruling, not a header tweak.
options.gate: Nothing in @theme changes; the override is a class the build would emit, scoped to the header. `check:render’s oracle reads warm ink on paper at 12.37, so this row is expected to pass the shipped gate.

Then re-quote the 217px figure: it is the 320 number, and this option grows the row above 640 (measured in the record).
